name: Glitch / datamosh / VHS
look: broken codec blocks, RGB split, pixel smears, tracking noise, scan tears.

fits.notes: AI, security, music, gaming, "something broke" stories, bold challenger. Overused as "tech" shorthand

products: reliability brands unless the glitch is the story

when_not: Overused as "tech" shorthand; avoid for reliability brands unless the glitch is the story.

type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: mono or grotesk; cyan/magenta/black; white timecode.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: brand colour replaces cyan or magenta in the split; black and white around
brand_lock.type_role: mono or grotesk; white timecode; brand face for the claim, never glitched past legibility
brand_lock.world_changes: the film breaks and reforms around the product
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: datamosh smear between scenes (motion vectors dragged over the next scene)
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects.role: scene-change datamosh: pass the outgoing frame with setPrev

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: a deliberately broken frame of {subject}: codec block corruption, RGB split, scan tears

animate_with.what: displacement / warp (shader fed by noise or depth)

codex_assets.r1_note: no need; stills can be glitched as plates if you want custom "broken" frames.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

build.recipe: `library/motion/glitch/glitch-datamosh.md`; implement in GLSL: block-hash displacement + chroma split, accumulation buffer for smear (Three.js with render targets, seek-safe via seeded hashes on `floor(t*fps)`). Apple-keynote-clean otherwise.

examples.title: "The Glitch" (BBDO, Alzheimer Forschung Initiative, datamosh transitions)

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

palettes.name: VHS
palettes.words: tape black, white, scan red, cyan fringe

palettes.name: Signal lost
palettes.words: black, pale phosphor white, neon green, magenta

palettes.name: Newsroom error
palettes.words: navy black, white, caution yellow, red

brand_lock.rule: Brand colour is the glitch's displaced channel (replace one of red/cyan in the split) only when it has enough chroma; never let the logo be glitched, hold it clean. Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Mono display with RGB-split text-shadow (±0.4%), timestamp captions.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

passes.role: block shifts, tears, RGB split on cut frames only

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...).

composition.grid: full-frame source image with 4:3 tape bleed; glitch events as horizontal bands and blocks 8-40 px
composition.safe_area: none: tracking noise at the bottom 6% and a timestamp top-right
composition.product_ui: UI is shown as a corrupted-then-resolved screen: glitch resolves to clean on the proof beat

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: consumer camcorder 4:3, soft focus, slight handheld, auto-exposure pumping. Lighting: harsh on-camera flash or fluorescent, blown highlights. Material: video artefacts: tracking lines, chroma bleed, block compression, field interlacing. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: heavy analog noise, scanlines, tape dropouts. Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no clean digital look, no perfect alignment, no readable text corruption of key words, no colour gradients.
codex.camera: consumer camcorder 4:3, soft focus, slight handheld, auto-exposure pumping
codex.lighting: harsh on-camera flash or fluorescent, blown highlights
codex.material: video artefacts: tracking lines, chroma bleed, block compression, field interlacing
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.
codex.texture: heavy analog noise, scanlines, tape dropouts
negatives: no readable text corruption of key words

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: video artefacts: tracking lines; consumer camcorder 4:3; tape black, white, scan red, cyan fringe.

sprite_sheet.rules: Not a sprite style. For a cut-out object or character use --transparent (flat #00FF00 key, then despill); one subject, no shadow plane.

do: Glitch on the cut, resolve on the proof
Keep the logo and claim clean
Use 3-5 distinct artefacts (tear, block, smear, split), not one
dont: Do not use more than 2 accent colours
cheap_ways: Constant jitter on everything reads as a free preset
Neon cyberpunk palette for an unrelated product
